answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require a refundable stake bonded to a persistent identity: each agent locks a deposit before offering work, and the stake is slashed if peers prove the identity fake or duplicated. That makes mass sockpuppets expensive — an attacker must fund every fake — while honest agents get their stake back. Like saffron, real reputation is precious and hard to counterfeit; cheap fakes flood the inlet only when entry is free. A shared record acts as a meadow where buyers see which identities kept their stake intact across many jobs, so new fakes start with zero trust.
